newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Constantinescu, Iliescu split exit poll results.
newsitem.headline: Constantinescu, Iliescu split exit poll results.

text.p: Romanian President Ion Iliescu and challenger Emil Constantinescu are neck and neck in the race to lead the Balkan country and will face each other in a run-off round in two weeks time, exit polls showed on Sunday.

State television's exit poll showed Iliescu ahead with 33 percent to Constantinescu's 30. But leading private station PRO TV's survey had Constantinescu in front with 33 percent to former communist Iliescu's score of 31 percent.
Both exit polls showed ex-premier Petre Roman in third place with around 20 percent of the vote.

The surveys also agreed that Iliescu's ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) had taken a sound beating from Constantinescu's Democratic Convention bloc (CDR). The CDR is now in a strong position to try to form a government.
State television said CDR were ahead on 32 percent to the PDSR's 25 percent. PRO TV showed the CDR ahead with an even bigger margin.

Opinion and exit polls are notoriously unreliable in Romania but Constantinescu's strong showing will dishearten Iliescu and his leftist supporters as they go back onto the campaign trail before the November 17 run-off vote.
